❓ Frequently asked questions

What is a factorial?

n! (n factorial) is the product of all positive integers from 1 to n. For example, 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120. By definition, 0! = 1.

Why is the maximum 170?

170! is the largest factorial that fits in a standard 64-bit floating-point number (about 7.26 × 10^306). 171! overflows to infinity.

How are trailing zeros counted?

Each trailing zero comes from a factor of 10 = 2 × 5. Since factors of 2 are plentiful, the count equals the number of factors of 5 in 1…n: floor(n/5) + floor(n/25) + floor(n/125) + …
